div.head: ECf retr Rb I
div.ab: Primum capitulum hoc est: Incipiunt leges sancti Edwardi regis, quas in Anglia tenuit, et quas Willelmus, heres et cognatus suus, postea confirmauit.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 670 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

This is one of the chapter headings (rubrics) that a later writer, whom Liebermann calls “Rubricator II” and dates 1163–1189, made for the Retractator’s text. Liebermann prints them on pp. 670–672 as an appendix (Anhang) to ECf retr; they are numbered here “Rb” with his Roman numerals. He prints in small type what is taken from the text of ECf retr, so the words in bold are the Rubricator’s own.
Liebermann gives in the margin, in square brackets, the chapter of ECf retr that this heading belongs to: Prol..
The words “Hic … est” of note 2 run from “Hic” in the heading above to “est” in “Primum capitulum hoc est”; the note is given with both.

note.seg: Hic—est roth Lb, grösser Ra, am Rande Ph, fehlt Hv Vi Gr Lond; Inc. capitula l. s. Vi
